title: Underwriting & Sizing
intro: Upload a property’s T12, draft its underwriting — Safe and Aggressive, account by account, each change with its story — approve it, then see what you can still push and what loan each version supports.

topics.title: Open Underwriting
topics.intro: Underwriting opens in its own tab, from the “+” at the end of the tab strip.

steps.title: The “+” menu
steps.text: Click the “+” at the end of the tab strip. It lists the tools that open in a tab of their own.

marks.text: Opens this menu: a tool in a new tab.

marks.label: Underwriting & Sizing
marks.text: The T12, the underwriting (Safe and Aggressive), what to push and debt sizing — this chapter.

marks.label: Maturity & Reset Calendar
marks.text: Every maturity, rate reset and interest-only step-up, month by month.

marks.label: Data Health
marks.text: What is missing or needs a look, across the whole book.

steps.title: The Underwriting tab
steps.text: Underwriting opens as a tab next to Portfolio. Keep several tools open and switch between them; each tab can also open in a window of its own.

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the portfolio (Home).

marks.label: Underwriting
marks.text: This tab.

marks.label: Pop out
marks.text: Opens this tab in its own window — handy on a second screen.

marks.label: Close tab
marks.text: Closes the tab. Nothing is lost: the property’s T12, its underwriting and its approval are saved with the property.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property to underwrite. A property that already has a T12 loads it, with its underwriting.

marks.label: The T12 box
marks.text: Where the property’s T12 file goes (next topic).

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Empties this screen. The property’s saved files and figures stay.

topics.title: Upload a T12
topics.intro: Two ways: drag the file onto the box, or click “choose a file” and pick it from your computer. Excel and CSV exports are read; the T12 sheet is found by itself. Without a T12 there is no underwriting — and no refinance.

steps.title: Pick the property first
steps.text: Choose the property in the Property list. The T12 you upload is saved in that property’s folder, and read from there from now on.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property this T12 belongs to.

marks.label: Drag and drop
marks.text: Drag the T12 file from your folder (File Explorer) and let go over this box.

marks.label: choose a file
marks.text: Or click here: your computer’s file window opens — find the T12, click it, then Open.

steps.title: Read by the reader and the AI
steps.text: The file is saved to the property’s folder and read twice — by the app’s own reader and by Claude — before anything from it is used. When every check passes and both agree, it is used at once, and the underwriting draft starts from it by itself; otherwise a window shows you the rows and you decide (the Documents chapter shows that window in full).

marks.label: Setup built
marks.text: The file’s name, and that the table below was built from it.

marks.label: file verified
marks.text: The file was read in full and its totals tie to the statement.

marks.label: Checked by the reader and the AI
marks.text: Both readings agree — the figures are in use.

marks.label: Review the reading
marks.text: Opens how each row of the file was read (next step).

marks.label: Read again
marks.text: Reads the file again from the start.

marks.label: NOI used
marks.text: The in-place NOI the app uses from this file, and the months it covers.

steps.title: Review the reading
steps.text: Every row of the file as the reader read it: what it is (an account, a category, a total), income or expense, its category in the file, the underwriting line it lands on, the amount used, and a check against its months. You can change any of these, with a note; nothing is saved until you click Save.

marks.label: The verdict
marks.text: Whether every check passes and the AI agrees with the reader.

marks.label: What the reader made of it
marks.text: Account, category name, total, header… change it when the reader got a row wrong.

marks.label: Underwriting line
marks.text: The line of the Underwriting table this account adds to.

marks.label: Your note
marks.text: Why you changed a row — kept with the reading.

marks.label: Close without saving
marks.text: Closes the window and keeps the reading as it was.

marks.label: Save this reading
marks.text: Saves your changes; every figure from this T12 follows them.

topics.title: Units and rent
topics.intro: Three boxes under the file: the units, and the gross potential rent (a year’s figure, or the average rent per unit).

steps.title: Units, gross potential rent, average rent
steps.text: The units set the replacement reserves (taken off Safe and Aggressive) and every per-unit figure. A gross potential rent above the T12’s comes into the draft as a suggestion; leave it blank to keep the statement’s rent.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: How many apartments the property has (from the rent roll). Typing it here also asks to save it in the property’s profile.

marks.label: Gross potential rent — per year
marks.text: A year’s rent if every unit were leased at market, before vacancy. When it is above the T12’s rent, the draft suggests it (with its story) — never applied by itself.

marks.label: Average rent per unit — per month
marks.text: Easier than the yearly figure: the average monthly rent for one unit; the app works out average × units × 12.

topics.title: The underwriting table
topics.intro: Every line of the T12, classified: the statement’s figure (In-Place) and the underwriting (Safe or Aggressive), each per unit. The underwriting starts as the T12 less the reserves — a draft until you approve it.

steps.title: The three figures on top
steps.text: In-place NOI (the statement, by the T12 rule), and the Safe and Aggressive underwriting NOI (after the replacement reserves). Until you approve them they read “draft · not approved yet”.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The T12’s own NOI — the 12-month total, or the last 3 months × 4 when the statement starts in a lease-up.

marks.label: How it was worked out
marks.text: Which months it comes from.

marks.label: ties to statement NOI
marks.text: The lines add up to the NOI printed on the statement.

marks.label: Safe underwriting NOI
marks.text: The T12 with the changes you can defend line by line, less the reserves.

marks.label: Aggressive underwriting NOI
marks.text: Safe plus the changes a cautious lender may not accept, less the reserves.

marks.label: draft · not approved yet
marks.text: A draft until you approve it (its own topic); then it reads “approved” with the date.

steps.title: The columns
steps.text: Every line of the T12, classified (the line names are the app’s; the Documents chapter shows how each account was placed). Two figures per line — the T12 and the underwriting — each also per unit.

marks.label: Line
marks.text: The underwriting line; a line far from its benchmark is flagged next to its name.

marks.label: In-Place (T12)
marks.text: Each line as the statement shows it.

marks.label: $/unit
marks.text: The figure ÷ the units.

marks.label: Underwriting · Safe
marks.text: The underwriting, line by line, in the version the switch shows. Click any figure in it to open that line’s accounts.

marks.label: A figure
marks.text: Click it: the line’s accounts open, to change one by one (its own topic).

steps.title: The reserves and the NOI
steps.text: Subtotals for rental income, effective gross income and expenses, then the replacement reserves and the Net Operating Income — each in both columns and per unit.

marks.label: Effective Gross Income
marks.text: All income after vacancy and other deductions.

marks.label: Total Operating Expenses
marks.text: Every expense line added up.

marks.label: Replacement reserves
marks.text: Your reserves per unit × the units — a line in both Safe and Aggressive (the T12 has none).

marks.label: Net Operating Income
marks.text: In-place NOI, and the underwriting NOI after the reserves — each per unit.

topics.title: Draft the underwriting — its bar
topics.intro: Above the table, the underwriting’s bar: whether it is a draft or approved, the two versions, the tools to change it, and Approve.

steps.title: The bar
steps.text: Everything you do to the underwriting starts here. Nothing in it is used by the refinance, the roll-up or What to push until you approve it.

marks.label: draft
marks.text: Draft, approved, or changed since approved.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive
marks.text: Which version the column shows (next topic).

marks.label: The two NOIs
marks.text: Safe and Aggressive underwriting NOI, after the reserves.

marks.label: Suggestions
marks.text: Every open suggestion in one list.

marks.label: Claude’s stories…
marks.text: Jumps to Claude’s stories under the table (and asks Claude for them the first time).

marks.label: Revenue credit…
marks.text: Annualize all revenue accounts at once (its own topic).

marks.label: + Add an account
marks.text: An account the T12 doesn’t have (its own topic).

marks.label: For the lender…
marks.text: The Excel file for the lender.

marks.label: History
marks.text: Every change, with its story, and every approval.

marks.label: Start over
marks.text: Takes every change out and starts again from the T12 (asks first). The history keeps them, and the last approval stays in use until you approve again.

marks.label: Approve the underwriting
marks.text: Safe and Aggressive become this property’s underwriting (its own topic).

marks.label: Not approved yet
marks.text: What is in use: nothing yet.

steps.title: What to push waits for the approval
steps.text: Further down, What to push says so: it works from the approved Safe and Aggressive, so it runs only after you approve.

marks.label: Approve the underwriting first
marks.text: Approve, and Claude works out what you can still push (its own topic).

topics.title: Draft — Safe and Aggressive
topics.intro: Two versions. Safe: what you would defend line by line. Aggressive: Safe plus the changes a cautious lender may not accept.

steps.title: Two versions
steps.text: Aggressive starts as Safe and adds its own changes; a change made for Aggressive on an account wins over Safe’s in Aggressive. Every change says where it applies: Safe, Aggressive or Both. Use the switch to see either one in the column.

marks.label: Safe
marks.text: The column shows the Safe version.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: The column shows the Aggressive version.

marks.label: Both NOIs
marks.text: The one shown first, then the other.

steps.title: How each one adds up
steps.text: Under the table, one box per version: the T12 NOI, every change grouped by its kind with its story, the NOI before reserves, the replacement reserves, and the underwriting NOI — checked to the dollar.

marks.label: Safe — how it adds up
marks.text: T12 NOI + each change − reserves = the Safe underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Aggressive — how it adds up
marks.text: The same for Aggressive.

marks.label: reconciles to the dollar
marks.text: The changes add up exactly (worked out twice).

marks.label: − Replacement reserves
marks.text: Your reserves per unit × the units, taken off both versions.

marks.label: = Safe underwriting NOI
marks.text: The figure that is approved, sized and refinanced on.

topics.title: Draft — a line’s accounts
topics.intro: Click a figure in the Underwriting column: a window opens with every account of that line.

steps.title: Every account, every month
steps.text: The window is about 80% of the screen. On top, the line in the T12, in Safe and in Aggressive. Below, every account of the line — none hidden, a $0 one too — with its 12 months as the statement shows them.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: The whole line in the T12, in Safe and in Aggressive, each per unit.

marks.label: An account
marks.text: Its row in the file, its 12 months, its T12, Safe and Aggressive. Click it to change it.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: The account’s year in the statement.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive
marks.text: The account in each version.

marks.label: A $0 account
marks.text: Shown with its twelve zeros — nothing is hidden.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: Each month and each column added up.

marks.label: + Add an account the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: For money the statement has no account for.
Closes the window.

topics.title: Draft — change an account
topics.intro: Click an account and its choices open right under it. Each change has a kind, the version it applies to and a story.

steps.title: The choices
steps.text: New amount (0 takes the account out), Spread over years, Annualize, % of revenue and Per unit. The next topics show each one.

marks.label: New amount
marks.text: Type the account’s new yearly figure. Type 0 to take it out — it reads “Took out” for the lender.

marks.label: Spread over years
marks.text: A cost paid once every few years counts only its share for one year.

marks.label: Annualize
marks.text: The account becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months.

marks.label: % of revenue
marks.text: The account set as a % of revenue (expenses and rental deductions).

marks.label: Per unit
marks.text: A dollar figure per apartment per year × the units.

steps.title: A new amount, its kind and its story
steps.text: Snow removal set to $9,000 for a normal winter. Pick the kind, where it applies, and write the story the lender reads — or pick one you already wrote. The preview shows the account’s 12 months before and after, the line and the NOI.

marks.label: Its new amount
marks.text: The yearly figure for this account.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Why it changes: non-recurring, spread, normalized, operating change, market norm, partnership/back-office (and revenue credit when annualizing income).

marks.label: Apply to
marks.text: Safe, Aggressive or Both.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads. Required.

marks.label: Draft it with Claude
marks.text: Claude writes a first draft from the account’s months; you edit it.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: The account’s 12 months in the T12 and after the change (each month in proportion).

marks.label: ready to save
marks.text: Or what is still missing.

marks.label: Save the change
marks.text: Saves it; the window stays open on this line.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the choices without saving.

steps.title: Saved
steps.text: The account shows its new figure in Safe and Aggressive, and a tag with where it applies and its kind. The line’s totals follow.

marks.label: The changed account
marks.text: Now 9,000 in Safe and Aggressive; at the right end of its row, a tag says where it applies and its kind (hover it for the story).

marks.label: The line
marks.text: Now $27,500 in both versions.

steps.title: Edit or remove a change
steps.text: Click a changed account again: its changes are listed on top, each with Edit and Remove, who made it and when.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: What, kind, story, who and when, and its effect on the NOI.

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens it with its figures to change.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Removes it (asks first); the history keeps it.

steps.title: Same story as…
steps.text: One cause often moves several accounts. Pick a story you already wrote and it fills in — then adjust it if you want.

marks.label: Same story as…
marks.text: The stories already in this underwriting, with their account.

topics.title: Draft — spread, annualize, % of revenue, per unit
topics.intro: The other ways to change an account.

steps.title: Spread over years
steps.text: For a cost paid once every few years that landed in this T12. Exterior painting cost $14,400 in May and is done every 5 years: the underwriting counts $14,400 ÷ 5 = $2,880 a year. It divides the whole account — for an account that mixes normal monthly costs with one big bill, use New amount instead.

marks.label: Paid every … years
marks.text: How often it is paid; it counts one share a year.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Set to “Spread over years” by itself.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: $14,400 in May becomes $2,880 for the year.

steps.title: Annualize
steps.text: When an account runs differently in its recent months — a new contract, a rent increase — it becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months. Each choice shows what it gives; the last 12 months on a normal 12-month T12 is the T12 itself, so it is greyed (“same as the T12”).

marks.label: Last 3 months
marks.text: × 4 — here $28,400 a year.

marks.label: Last 12 months
marks.text: Only different from the T12 when the file has more than 12 months, or the T12 rule used the last 3 months × 4.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: The months it comes from.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Operating change for an expense; Revenue credit for an income account.

steps.title: % of revenue
steps.text: The account set as a % of revenue: an expense as a % of that version’s effective gross income, a rental deduction (vacancy, bad debt) as a % of gross potential rent. Because you chose it, it moves when that version’s revenue moves — the management fee never moves by itself.

marks.text: The percentage.

marks.label: It follows revenue
marks.text: Only because you picked % of revenue.

marks.label: The management fee
marks.text: Stays at the T12 unless you change its account.

steps.title: Per unit
steps.text: A dollar figure per apartment per year, times the units (120 here) — for a cost quoted per unit, like a maintenance role or turnover.

marks.label: $ per unit a year
marks.text: × the property’s units.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: Here only in the Aggressive version.

marks.label: Preview
marks.text: Safe unchanged; Aggressive $300 × 120 = $36,000.

topics.title: Draft — suggestions from your assumptions
topics.intro: When a line runs worse than your assumption (or the rent roll proves more rent), its biggest account gets a suggestion with a ready story. A suggestion only ever raises the NOI, and nothing is applied by itself.

steps.title: A suggestion on the account
steps.text: The management fee runs 3% of revenue; your assumption is 2.5%. Its account carries a “Suggested” chip; open it to see the suggestion and why.

marks.label: Suggested
marks.text: A suggestion is waiting on this account.

marks.label: The suggestion
marks.text: The change, its kind, the default story and why.

marks.label: Use this
marks.text: Fills the change and its story in — you can still edit before saving.

marks.label: Not this one
marks.text: Sets it aside (you can bring it back).

steps.title: Every suggestion in one list
steps.text: The “suggestions” button in the bar lists every open suggestion — from your assumptions and from Claude — each with “Open the account”.

marks.label: A suggestion
marks.text: Where, what and its story.

marks.label: Open the account
marks.text: Opens the line with the suggestion filled in.

topics.title: Draft — Claude’s stories
topics.intro: Under the table: Claude reads every account month by month and offers stories a lender would accept — only ones that raise the NOI.

steps.title: Claude’s stories for the underwriting
steps.text: Each card: the line and the account, the change and its kind, the story, how Claude got the number and what you need to back it with the lender, and how much it raises the NOI. Claude may not invent an event or a figure; a story that would lower the NOI is never offered — it is listed as left out.

marks.label: Find stories / Look again
marks.text: Asks Claude (it needs Claude connected).

marks.label: A story
marks.text: One account, one change, its story.

marks.label: How Claude got the number
marks.text: From the statement’s own figures.

marks.label: To back it
marks.text: What you need on hand to prove it.

marks.label: Put it in the draft
marks.text: Opens the account with it filled in, to check and save.

marks.label: In the pro forma ✓
marks.text: Already in the draft.

topics.title: Draft — add an account
topics.intro: For money the T12 has no account for — a PILOT tax, an antenna lease, bad debt at a market norm.

steps.title: Pick the line
steps.text: “+ Add an account” in the bar lists every line — the ones in your T12 first, then the ones it doesn’t have.

marks.label: A line the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: Adding an account here adds the line to the underwriting.

steps.title: Name it, its amount, its story
steps.text: Name the account, give its amount (or % of revenue, or per unit), the kind, where it applies and the story.

marks.label: Account name
marks.text: What the lender will see.

marks.label: Its amount
marks.text: A year’s figure.

marks.label: Preview
marks.text: Nothing in Safe; $500 a month in Aggressive.

topics.title: Draft — revenue credit
topics.intro: Every revenue account annualized at once from its last 3, 6 or 12 months — when the property runs better now than the year shows.

steps.title: Revenue credit
steps.text: Each revenue account becomes its last 3 months × 4 (or 6 × 2). The table shows every revenue line month by month, the months used highlighted, the T12 and the annualized figure; today’s occupancy from the rent roll if there is one. A story is required. The management fee does not follow it.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive (its own)
marks.text: Aggressive can have its own; until then it uses Safe’s.

marks.label: T3 / T6 / T12
marks.text: How many recent months. T12 changes nothing on a normal 12-month file.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: Which months.

marks.label: Annualized
marks.text: Each line after the credit.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads.

marks.label: Save the revenue credit
marks.text: Saves it.

topics.title: Assumptions, benchmarks and warnings
topics.intro: The assumptions don’t change the underwriting by themselves: they give the draft its suggestions (only ones that raise the NOI), a warning when they would lower it, and the reserves.

steps.title: Assumptions, benchmarks, save
steps.text: Per property. A line that runs worse than an assumption gets a suggestion in the draft; the reserves per unit are taken off Safe and Aggressive. Each change is kept in the property’s history.

marks.label: Vacancy
marks.text: When the T12 runs above it, the vacancy account gets a suggestion at it; when the T12 already runs below it, a warning — never applied by itself.

marks.label: Management fee
marks.text: As a % of effective gross income — a suggestion when the T12 runs above it, a warning when it would lower the NOI.

marks.label: Reserves / unit
marks.text: Replacement reserves a year per unit — taken off Safe and Aggressive.

marks.label: Payroll / unit
marks.text: Your payroll benchmark for this property; a payroll line 15% off it is flagged.

marks.label: R&M / unit
marks.text: Your repairs & maintenance benchmark.

marks.label: Save to property record
marks.text: Saves the assumptions and benchmarks with the property, so every screen uses them.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to these, old → new, who and when.

steps.title: An assumption that would lower the NOI — a warning
steps.text: Here the management fee assumption is set to 4%, but the T12 runs 3%. That would lower the NOI, so it is never a suggestion: the bar warns you, for information, and the underwriting keeps the T12’s figure. To underwrite 4% anyway, change the account yourself, with its story.

marks.label: The warning
marks.text: Your assumption, what the T12 runs, and how much lower the NOI would be at your assumption.

marks.label: The NOIs
marks.text: Unchanged — an assumption never moves the underwriting by itself.

topics.title: Draft — the result, the lender file, history
topics.intro: The column and how it adds up after the changes; the Excel file for the lender; every change’s history.

steps.title: The column after the changes
steps.text: Changed lines are outlined with a teal dot; hover one to see its kinds. The NOI rows follow.

marks.label: A changed line
marks.text: Teal dot: this line has changes.

marks.label: Underwriting NOI
marks.text: In the NOI row, after the reserves.

steps.title: How it adds up
steps.text: T12 NOI + the revenue credit + each account change, grouped by kind with its story, less the reserves = the underwriting NOI, for Safe and for Aggressive.

marks.label: Revenue credit
marks.text: The credit’s effect.

marks.label: Normalized
marks.text: Snow removal, with its story.

marks.label: − Replacement reserves
marks.text: Taken off both versions.

marks.label: = Safe underwriting NOI
marks.text: What you approve next.

steps.title: For the lender — the Excel file
steps.text: Safe only, or Safe and Aggressive. The file has four sheets: Pro forma (each line with its change, kind and story, and the reserves), Changed accounts, Reconciliation and Monthly (the months used for the revenue credit marked).

marks.label: Safe only
marks.text: One version.

marks.label: Safe and Aggressive
marks.text: Both, side by side.

marks.label: Save the Excel file…
marks.text: Asks where to save “<property> — Pro forma — <date>.xlsx”.

steps.title: History
steps.text: Every change, edit, removal and set-aside, newest first: which line and account, old → new, the kind and story, who and when. Each approval is kept here too.

marks.label: An entry
marks.text: One change with its story.
Closes it.

topics.title: Approve the underwriting
topics.intro: Approving makes Safe and Aggressive this property’s underwriting: the refinance, the portfolio roll-up and What to push work from them. Change the draft later and approve again.

steps.title: Approve
steps.text: When Safe and Aggressive are what you would show — every change with its story, both adding up to the dollar — click Approve the underwriting.

marks.label: draft
marks.text: Not approved yet.

marks.label: Approve the underwriting
marks.text: Approves both versions as they are now — who and when are kept.

steps.title: Approved
steps.text: The chip reads “approved”, and the line under the bar says who approved it, when, and the figures now in use.

marks.label: approved
marks.text: This is the property’s underwriting.

marks.label: Approved by …
marks.text: Who, when, and the Safe and Aggressive NOI the refinance, the roll-up and What to push use.

steps.title: The figures on top say so
steps.text: The Safe and Aggressive cards read “approved” with the date.

marks.label: approved
marks.text: Safe, as approved.

marks.label: approved
marks.text: Aggressive, as approved.

steps.title: A change after the approval
steps.text: Change anything that moves Safe or Aggressive — here the reserves go to $250 a unit — and the chip reads “changed since approved”. Until you approve again, everything keeps using the figures you approved.

marks.label: changed since approved
marks.text: The draft no longer matches what was approved.

marks.label: What is still in use
marks.text: The approved figures, and who approved them when.

marks.label: Approve again
marks.text: Approves the draft as it is now; What to push runs again on it.

topics.title: What to push
topics.intro: After the approval: what you can still push from the approved underwriting — things not proven yet, so not stories in it — measured on the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive.

steps.title: Claude’s pushes
steps.text: It runs by itself once the underwriting is approved (Claude must be connected), and again when you approve again. Each push only raises the NOI, never pulls a lever a story already pulls (one that sits beside a story names it), and shows its effect three ways, each net of what that version already counts. These are your plan, not the lender’s: tick them in the refinance to see what loan they would get you.

marks.label: Re-analyse
marks.text: Asks Claude again.

marks.label: A push
marks.text: What to do, why (from this statement’s own figures) and the effort.

marks.label: Its effect, three ways
marks.text: On the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive — Claude’s estimates, a starting point, not advice.

marks.label: The lever
marks.text: What it moves — never one a story in the underwriting already moves.

marks.label: Beside the story
marks.text: The underwriting story it sits next to: a different lever, so both count.

topics.title: Debt sizing
topics.intro: The largest loan each version supports, side by side, at the limits you set for this property.

steps.title: Safe and Aggressive, side by side
steps.text: Each limit gives a loan amount on each version’s NOI; the smallest is the maximum supportable loan, and the limit that sets it “binds”. A quick answer while you underwrite — the refinance sizes the real loan with its lender’s own limits.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Max LTV
marks.text: The loan as a share of that value.

marks.label: Min DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ the yearly payment must be at least this.

marks.label: Min debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ the loan must be at least this.

marks.label: Interest rate
marks.text: The rate the payment is worked out at.

topics.title: Operating history and the roll-up
topics.intro: The property’s months kept from every T12 with its approved underwriting, and the whole portfolio’s NOI and coverage in one table.

steps.title: General Data — operating history
steps.text: Every T12 you upload adds its months (up to 24 are kept). The card shows the in-place NOI and the approved underwriting (Safe · Aggressive); each line shows its trailing 12 months and the change against the 12 before.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The same NOI as everywhere in the app, and how it was worked out.

marks.label: Underwriting NOI — Safe · Aggressive
marks.text: The approved underwriting, and when it was approved (“not approved yet” before).

marks.label: Saved to the folder
marks.text: Kept in the property’s folder (general-data.json).

marks.label: Trailing 12-mo
marks.text: Each line’s last 12 months, and its change.

steps.title: Portfolio roll-up
steps.text: Every property: units, loans, in-place NOI, the approved Safe underwriting NOI (blank until approved), balance, yearly debt service, DSCR, debt yield, LTV and maturity — with the total row. Click a property to underwrite it.
